answer: To enforce an anti-Sybil equilibrium, the pearl protocol mandates quadratic slashing on staking collateral, escalating marginal attack costs super-linearly with each added node. Using falcon signatures and zero-knowledge delay functions, the tundra engine verifies identity and enforces an economic security threshold that guarantees negative expected utility for malicious actors. As a result, the cost of acquiring sufficient consensus weight to execute a double-spend structurally outpaces any extractable value, sustaining a robust Nash equilibrium.
